statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The Sunday restart has now held the 29,530.50-29,595.25 band for a fifth hour while volume roughly doubled again to about 14.2k contracts, and NQ last printed 29,565.25, exactly Friday's settle. A 2.0% Nikkei advance on AI and memory names has not pulled NQ into extension, which is a rotational rather than one-way signature. Tail holds at the low-band floor. Stress stays elevated on the war-premium energy complex, a restrictive Treasury curve with a live September hike debate, and a holiday-thinned Monday that halts early.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European cash close into the early Labor Day futures halt, and secondarily in the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, rather than across the whole outlook; every forecast hour maps below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures sit exactly on Friday's settle after five hours inside a 65-point restart band, with a 2% Nikkei rally and a contained oil response failing to produce directional structure
body:
The Sunday restart is roughly five hours old and the observed price path still has not extended. NQ front-month last printed 29,565.25, identical to Friday's 4 September settle, inside a session range of 29,530.50 to 29,595.25 that is about 65 points or 0.22% wide. Volume has roughly doubled again to about 14.2k contracts since the previous assessment. Depth building while the range does not is the signature of orderly two-way price discovery rather than the directional efficiency that overwhelms mean reversion, and it is the single most important observation in this assessment.

The more interesting development is a divergence that did not transmit. The Nikkei 225 is up 2.0% at 66,319 with technology and AI-linked names leading, echoing Friday's US semiconductor strength where the whole chip complex closed higher. That strength has not pulled NQ out of its band. An index that declines to follow a 2% regional tech rally into new highs is rotating, not trending, and rotation is the environment in which mean reversion works.

The weekend geopolitical escalation remains contained. US Central Command struck three Iranian oil tankers on 5 September after the Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at a US carrier and destroyer, and Iran retaliated against tankers it said were using unauthorised routes near the Strait of Hormuz. Brent trades at 96.70 and WTI at 91.98, up 0.43% and 0.55% respectively, and OPEC+ separately left October quotas unchanged at 31.1 million barrels per day as expected. Both benchmarks were already war-elevated from roughly $70 before the strait was effectively closed in February, so this reads as a chronic, largely priced conflict rather than a fresh discontinuity. That is why the escalation supports Stress and not Tail.

Cross-asset alignment is absent. Friday's VIX close of 14.53 is low in absolute terms, the H.15 curve is restrictive but stable with the two-year at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77%, and the delayed cross-asset context shows index, rate, gold and volatility futures all within a few tenths of a percent of unchanged. Friday's Nasdaq internals were split rather than aligned, with semiconductors sharply higher while most megacaps fell. No shallow-pullback pattern, failed retracement or extreme-holding behaviour has been observed, so Tail sits at the low-band floor.

Monday is Labor Day. US cash equity markets are closed and CME equity index futures halt at 17:00 UTC with no Monday settlement published, reopening at 22:00 UTC for the Tuesday trade date. That produces a session with no domestic cash backstop, a thin book, and a hard stop that concentrates position squaring into a single hour, which is why the danger window is placed at 15:00-17:00 UTC rather than spread across the day.

The rate backdrop is the other elevated-Stress component. August payrolls printed 162,000 against a consensus near 53,000 on 4 September, reviving September hike expectations that Governor Waller had cooled the day before, and market odds for the 16 September decision sit close to a coin flip. August CPI on 11 September at 12:30 UTC is the decisive input and sits outside this outlook window, but it keeps forward Stress elevated throughout.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Tail held a flat 5 through the closed-venue Sunday hours, with a single 4 at 02:00 UTC, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout, then stepped to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart hour to carry reopen-gap risk before easing to 6 and back to 5 once the restart proved orderly. Stress ran from 54 through a 52-58 band to a 60 high at 20:00 UTC as Sunday's geopolitical flow accumulated, then eased to 57, 56 and 55 after the reopen. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every available hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the remainder of the Sunday restart, the rest of the Asian session, a European session traded against a closed US market on Labor Day, a shortened futures session that halts at 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, and the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band for every hour: 5 through the Asian hours now that the restart has proved contained, 6 at the Tokyo close, 7 across the European open and morning where the weekend Iran headlines first meet real depth without a US cash backstop, 6 to 7 through the holiday-thinned midday, 8 as the danger window opens at the European cash close and a peak of 9 in the final hour before the early halt, the closed-venue floor of 5 while futures are shut, then 8 at the Tuesday restart easing to 7 and 6. Stress holds in a 54-58 elevated band and confidence decays from 86 to 74 with forecast distance. The danger window is deliberately narrow at 15:00-17:00 UTC.
